quote: Code, identifiers and commit messages are in English.
statement: In all source files, identifiers (variables, functions, types, files) must be written in English.

quote: Write one block per concept, with the three languages in the order `EN`, `PT`, `ES`, not a translation of every line.
statement: In all mini-project and tool source files, explanatory comments must be written as one block per concept with three language sections prefixed `EN:`, `PT:`, `ES:` in that order (English first), not a line-by-line translation.
scope: projects/**, benchmarks/**, tools/**, quiz/** source files (comments)

quote: Every place that has Portuguese has Spanish too: comments, READMEs (`README.es.md` next to `README.pt-BR.md`), `docs/es/` next to `docs/pt/`, and the `es` block of every quiz question.
statement: In all source files, every `PT:` comment block must be accompanied by an `ES:` comment block (checked by .claude/scripts/check-es.ts).

quote: Spanish is neutral Latin American Spanish (`tú`, not `vos` or `vosotros`).
statement: In all Spanish comments and texts, the Spanish must be neutral Latin American Spanish using `tú`, not `vos` or `vosotros`.
scope: ** ES: comment blocks and Spanish content

quote: Strong typing: no `any` (use `unknown` and narrow)
statement: In TypeScript files, code must not use the `any` type; use `unknown` and narrow it instead.

quote: explicit return types on exported functions.
statement: In TypeScript files, exported functions must declare an explicit return type.

quote: Never silence an error with `@ts-ignore` or by disabling a test.
statement: In TypeScript files, code must never use `@ts-ignore` to silence a type error.

quote: Never silence an error with `@ts-ignore` or by disabling a test.
statement: In test files, tests must not be disabled (e.g. `test.skip`, `it.skip`, commented-out tests) to silence a failure.

quote: Validate every external input (JSON files, HTTP bodies, environment variables) at the boundary with **Zod**, the default schema library of this repository
statement: In TypeScript code, every external input (JSON files, HTTP request bodies, environment variables) must be validated at the boundary with a `zod` schema.
scope: **/*.ts code reading JSON files, HTTP bodies or env vars

quote: Derive the TypeScript types from the schemas with `z.infer` instead of writing them twice.
statement: In TypeScript code, types for validated data must be derived from the Zod schema with `z.infer<typeof schema>` rather than declared separately.

quote: Do not hand-write validators.
statement: In TypeScript code, input validation must not be implemented with hand-written validator functions; use Zod schemas.

quote: Every vulnerable example ships with its fixed version and an automated test proving the fix.
statement: In security mini-projects, every vulnerable example must ship together with a fixed version and an automated test proving the fix.

quote: Labs run only locally, in Docker, with no external network access.
statement: In security labs, services must run only locally in Docker with no external network access.

quote: No payloads aimed at real systems, no evasion techniques, no attack tooling reusable outside the lab.
statement: In security labs, code must not contain payloads aimed at real systems, evasion techniques (WAF/EDR/antivirus bypass) or attack tooling reusable outside the lab.

quote: Load and performance tests never target third-party URLs.
statement: In load and performance test scripts (k6 and similar), targets must be `localhost` or docker-compose service names of this repository, never third-party URLs.

quote: `.claude/skills/` holds Markdown only. Never add scripts, hooks or installers from the source repositories of those skills.
statement: In .claude/skills/**, only Markdown files (and LICENSE files) may exist; scripts, hooks, installers or binaries must not be added.

quote: **Dependencies:** pin exact stable versions. No `latest`, `next`, `rc`, `beta` or `alpha`.
statement: In package manifests (package.json, Cargo.toml, go.mod, requirements, mix.exs, build.gradle), dependencies must be pinned to exact stable versions; no ranges (`^`, `~`) and no `latest`, `next`, `canary`, `rc`, `beta` or `alpha` versions.

quote: Docker images use fixed version tags.
statement: In Dockerfiles and docker-compose files, images must use a fixed version tag, never `latest` or a pre-release tag.

quote: JS/TS uses Bun unless the mini-project is specifically about Node.js/npm.
statement: In JS/TS mini-projects, the runtime, package manager and test runner must be Bun (bun.lock, `bun test`) unless the mini-project is specifically about Node.js/npm.

quote: Setup scripts named `setup-unix-<project>.sh` and `setup-windows-<project>.ps1`. Everything runs in Docker with pinned images, so the scripts require only Docker.
statement: In each mini-project folder, setup scripts must be named `setup-unix-<project>.sh` and `setup-windows-<project>.ps1`.

quote: Three READMEs explaining what it teaches: `README.md` in English, `README.pt-BR.md` in Portuguese and `README.es.md` in Spanish, each linking to the other two on the line under the title.
statement: In each mini-project folder, `README.md`, `README.pt-BR.md` and `README.es.md` must exist, each linking to the other two under the title.

quote: Automated tests.
statement: In each mini-project, automated tests must exist for its implementation(s).

quote: Mini-projects live in `projects/<area>/<mini-project>/`, with one subfolder per language (`ts/`, `go/`, `rust/`).
statement: Mini-projects must live at `projects/<area>/<mini-project>/` with one subfolder per language implementation (`ts/`, `go/`, `rust/`, `python/`, ...).

quote: TypeScript is the reference implementation, and other languages are added only where the lesson changes.
statement: In each mini-project, TypeScript (`ts/`) must be the reference implementation; other language subfolders are added only where the lesson changes.

quote: The dashboard is a static page (HTML + Tailwind CSS v4 reading the results JSON). Next.js only where the concept needs a server.
statement: In mini-project dashboards, the dashboard must be a static HTML page styled with Tailwind CSS v4 that reads the results JSON; Next.js is used only where the concept needs a server.

quote: Everything runs in Docker, with pinned image versions. Setup scripts require only Docker. A local toolchain is optional
statement: In mini-project setup scripts, builds and tests must run inside Docker with pinned images; the scripts must require only Docker on the host, not a local language toolchain.

quote: Prefer the official `oven/bun` images for JS/TS projects.
statement: In JS/TS mini-project Dockerfiles, the base image should be an official `oven/bun` image.

quote: Ask the owner before adding a dependency that is not in the stack above.
statement: In mini-projects, dependencies outside the agreed stack must not be added without the owner's approval.

quote: PowerShell setup scripts use `$ErrorActionPreference = "Continue"` and check `$LASTEXITCODE` after each step, because Windows PowerShell 5.1 treats Docker's stderr output as an error.
statement: In PowerShell setup scripts, `$ErrorActionPreference = "Continue"` must be set and `$LASTEXITCODE` must be checked after each step.

quote: A static dashboard commits its built `tailwind.css`. Rebuild it with `bun run dashboard:css <dashboard folder>`.
statement: In static dashboards, the built `tailwind.css` must be committed next to the page.

quote: The page loads data through `<script src>` files, not `fetch`, so it works when opened from disk.
statement: In static dashboard pages, data must be loaded through `<script src>` files and must not be loaded with `fetch`.

quote: A mini-project never imports code from another one. Copy what it needs and say so in the README.
statement: In projects/<area>/<mini-project>/**, code must never import code from another mini-project's folder.

quote: Playwright: the package and the Docker image must have the same version.
statement: In projects using Playwright, the `playwright`/`@playwright/test` package version must equal the version tag of the Playwright Docker image.

quote: Unique docker-compose project name, no fixed host port unless the demo needs one (then bound to `127.0.0.1`), and `docker compose down -v` at the end of a test run.
statement: In mini-project docker-compose files, each must declare a unique compose project `name`.

quote: no fixed host port unless the demo needs one (then bound to `127.0.0.1`)
statement: In mini-project docker-compose files, services must not publish fixed host ports unless the demo needs one, and any published port must be bound to `127.0.0.1`.

quote: and `docker compose down -v` at the end of a test run.
statement: In mini-project setup/test scripts using docker-compose, the run must end with `docker compose down -v`.

quote: **Containers that write into the mounted project folder run as the host user**: `user: "${HOST_UID:-1000}:${HOST_GID:-1000}"` in docker-compose, with `HOST_UID="$(id -u)"` and `HOST_GID="$(id -g)"` exported by the Unix setup script.
statement: In docker-compose files, services that write into the mounted project folder must set `user: "${HOST_UID:-1000}:${HOST_GID:-1000}"`, and the Unix setup script must export `HOST_UID="$(id -u)"` and `HOST_GID="$(id -g)"`.

quote: PostgreSQL: `pg_isready -h 127.0.0.1 -U <user> -d <db>`, over TCP, because during initialisation the server answers on the Unix socket only and then restarts.
statement: In docker-compose files, PostgreSQL health checks must use `pg_isready -h 127.0.0.1 -U <user> -d <db>` over TCP.

quote: RabbitMQ: `nc -z 127.0.0.1 5672`, not `rabbitmq-diagnostics`, which runs as root and can create the Erlang cookie before the broker does, making the broker exit.
statement: In docker-compose files, RabbitMQ health checks must use `nc -z 127.0.0.1 5672` and must not use `rabbitmq-diagnostics`.

quote: Commit `setup-unix-<name>.sh` with the executable bit: `git update-index --chmod=+x <file>`.
statement: Unix setup scripts `setup-unix-<name>.sh` must be committed with the executable bit set.

quote: App in `quiz/`: Next.js with static site generation (SSG), Base UI (`@base-ui/react`) for the interactive components and Tailwind CSS v4 for the styling, no back end. Progress is stored in the browser.
statement: In quiz/, the app must be a statically generated Next.js app with no back end (no API routes or server actions); progress is stored in the browser.

quote: Interactive controls (buttons, toggles, selects, meters, popups) are Base UI components styled with Tailwind classes built from the theme tokens of `quiz/src/app/globals.css`, never a raw colour and never a hand-rolled widget
statement: In quiz React components, interactive controls (buttons, toggles, selects, meters, popups) must be Base UI components from `@base-ui/react`, never hand-rolled widgets.

quote: styled with Tailwind classes built from the theme tokens of `quiz/src/app/globals.css`, never a raw colour
statement: In quiz components, styling must use Tailwind classes built from the theme tokens defined in `quiz/src/app/globals.css` and must never use raw colour values (hex, rgb, or default palette colours).

quote: Links stay links, and static markup is not wrapped in Base UI.
statement: In quiz components, navigation links must remain links (`<a>`/Next `Link`) and static markup must not be wrapped in Base UI components.

quote: Three features are mandatory: i18n in English, Portuguese and Spanish, a light and dark theme toggle, and a mobile-friendly layout (usable from 320 px wide).
statement: In the quiz app, the UI must support i18n in en/pt/es, a light/dark theme toggle and a mobile layout usable from 320 px wide.

quote: Questions in `quiz/content/<area>/<topic>.json`, validated by a schema.
statement: Quiz questions must be stored in `quiz/content/<area>/<topic>.json` and conform to the quiz schema.

quote: Every question has exactly **5 alternatives**, one correct, a difficulty (`basic`, `intermediate`, `advanced`), a `source` (book or lecture and chapter) and, when one exists, the related `miniProject`.
statement: In quiz question JSON, every question must have exactly 5 alternatives with one correct `answer` index (0-4), a `difficulty` of `basic`|`intermediate`|`advanced`, a `source`, and a `miniProject` when one exists.

quote: Every question is written in **English, Portuguese and Spanish** at the same time (blocks `en`, `pt`, `es`). The schema refuses a question with a missing language.
statement: In quiz question JSON, every question must contain `en`, `pt` and `es` blocks.

quote: **A statement never depends on `example`.** The example belongs to the explanation and is shown only after the answer. Code, tables, graphs or schedules needed to answer go in `snippet`
statement: In quiz questions, the statement must never depend on `example`; material needed to answer must go in `snippet` or the statement.

quote: **Correct index**: spread it evenly and pseudo-randomly over 0 to 4. A fixed rotation (+1 per question) is a pattern a student can learn.
statement: In quiz content, the correct `answer` index should be spread evenly and pseudo-randomly over 0-4 within an area, not as a fixed rotation.

quote: **Length**: the correct alternative must not be the longest more often than chance (about 20%).
statement: In quiz content, the correct alternative must not be the longest alternative more often than about 20% of questions in an area.

quote: **SEO files are generated, never hand-edited.** `sitemap.xml`, `robots.txt`, `llms.txt` and `llms-full.txt` come from `quiz/src/app/` at every `next build`, using the validated areas (builders in `quiz/src/lib/seo.ts`
statement: In quiz/, `sitemap.xml`, `robots.txt`, `llms.txt` and `llms-full.txt` must be generated from route files in `quiz/src/app/` using builders in `quiz/src/lib/seo.ts`; no hand-written copies may be added under `quiz/public/`.

quote: The file name is the topic slug, and it must exist in `coverage.json`.
statement: In quiz/content/<area>/, each question file must be named `<topic-slug>.json` and the slug must exist in that area's `coverage.json`.

quote: `id` | `<area>-<topic>-<nn>`, unique in the whole quiz, never reused.
statement: In quiz question JSON, each question `id` must follow `<area>-<topic>-<nn>` and be unique across the whole quiz.

quote: `explanations` | exactly 5, in the same order: explanation `i` says why alternative `i` is right or wrong
statement: In quiz question JSON, each language block must have exactly 5 distinct `alternatives` and exactly 5 `explanations` in the same order.

quote: Present in all three languages or in none
statement: In quiz question JSON, `snippet` and `example` must be present in all three language blocks (`en`, `pt`, `es`) or in none.

quote: `miniProject` | optional. A path listed in `mini-projects.json`. Required when the concept is shown by a mini-project
statement: In quiz question JSON, `miniProject` must be a path listed in `quiz/content/mini-projects.json`.

quote: At least 3 sections. The `id` is an English kebab-case slug, unique in the file.
statement: In quiz theory summaries, there must be at least 3 sections and each section `id` must be a unique English kebab-case slug.

quote: The three languages have the same skeleton: the same section ids in the same order and, in each section, the same block types in the same order. Only the words change.
statement: In quiz theory summaries, `en.json`, `pt.json` and `es.json` must share the same section ids in the same order and the same block types in the same order per section.

quote: Table headers cannot be empty, and `*italic*` is not a mark (use `**bold**`).
statement: In quiz theory summaries, `table` blocks must not have empty headers (and every row has one cell per header), and text must not use `*italic*`; use `**bold**`.

quote: Inside any text four marks are read, and nothing else (HTML stays as plain text): `**bold**`, `` `code` ``, `[text](https://...)` and `[[term|meaning]]`
statement: In quiz theory text, only the marks `**bold**`, `` `code` ``, `[text](https://...)` and `[[term|meaning]]` may be used; HTML is not rendered.

quote: `video` | `title`, `url` (https) | a link to a video, from `REFERENCES.md` or opened and confirmed by the author. It is a link, not an embedded player
statement: In quiz theory summaries, `video` blocks must have an https `url` and are rendered as links, not embedded players.

quote: Use an `internal: true` network in docker-compose and bind published ports to `127.0.0.1`.
statement: In security lab docker-compose files, services must be on a network with `internal: true` and any published port must be bound to `127.0.0.1`.

quote: Every vulnerable example ships together with its **fixed version** and an **automated test** that fails against the vulnerable code and passes against the fix.
statement: In security labs, each vulnerable example must have an automated test that fails against the vulnerable version and passes against the fixed version.

quote: Vulnerable code is clearly labelled as such in file names, comments and the README, and is never importable as a library by other mini-projects.
statement: In security labs, vulnerable code must be labelled as vulnerable in its file names and comments.

quote: and is never importable as a library by other mini-projects.
statement: Outside its own lab folder, no mini-project may import vulnerable security-lab code as a library.

quote: No real credentials, tokens or personal data, even as examples. Use obviously fake values.
statement: In security labs (and examples), code must not contain real credentials, tokens or personal data; only obviously fake values.

quote: The target comes from a variable that defaults to a local address. Scripts must refuse to run when the host is not local.
statement: In k6 and load-test scripts, the target must come from a variable defaulting to a local address, and the script must refuse to run when the host is not local.

quote: Cross-language benchmarks follow one contract: every implementation reads the same input and prints JSON with at least `n`, elapsed time and memory.
statement: In cross-language benchmark implementations, each program must read the same input and print JSON with at least `n`, elapsed time and memory.

quote: Every benchmark records the machine, runtime versions and the exact command, so results are reproducible.
statement: In benchmark results, each benchmark must record the machine, runtime versions and exact command used.

quote: Never commit secrets, `.env` files, Terraform state, or `.claude/settings.local.json`.
statement: In the repository tree, secrets, `.env` files, Terraform state (`*.tfstate`) and `.claude/settings.local.json` must never be committed.

quote: Go `misspell` reads Spanish words as English typos: add them to `ignore-rules` in the module's `.golangci.yml`.
statement: In Go modules, Spanish/Portuguese comment words flagged by `misspell` must be added to `linters.settings.misspell.ignore-rules` in the module's `.golangci.yml`.

quote: its `workflow-sync` test fails when `ci.yml` gains a named step that the lesson does not demonstrate: a new gate needs a `demo/<gate>/` folder, the runner case and the READMEs.
statement: When `.github/workflows/ci.yml` gains a named step, `projects/continuous-integration/ci-pipeline` must have a matching `demo/<gate>/` folder and runner case.

quote: Bun closes a connection silent for 10 seconds, so a long request needs `idleTimeout`.
statement: In Bun servers handling requests that can stay silent longer than 10 seconds, `Bun.serve` must set `idleTimeout`.

quote: A watcher that reads a Prometheus ratio must treat `NaN` (0 / 0, no traffic yet) as a missing sample (`slo-alert`).
statement: In code reading Prometheus ratio queries, a `NaN` result must be treated as a missing sample rather than a value.

quote: **Imported content**: lives in `references/`, lowercase kebab-case paths.
statement: In references/, file and folder paths must be lowercase kebab-case.

quote: Lesson: a failure that looks like "slow runner" may be a property of random data; print the ids a test waits for.
statement: In tests that wait for randomly generated ids, the test should print the ids it waits for.

quote: [lint] select = ["E", ...] (pycodestyle errors)
statement: In Python files, code must pass ruff pycodestyle error rules (E).

quote: [lint] select = [..., "F", ...] (Pyflakes)
statement: In Python files, code must pass ruff Pyflakes rules (F): no unused imports/variables, undefined names, etc.

quote: [lint] select = [..., "W", ...] (pycodestyle warnings)
statement: In Python files, code must pass ruff pycodestyle warning rules (W).

quote: [lint] select = [..., "I", ...] (isort)
statement: In Python files, imports must be sorted according to ruff isort rules (I).

quote: [lint] select = [..., "B", ...] (flake8-bugbear)
statement: In Python files, code must pass ruff flake8-bugbear rules (B), e.g. no mutable default arguments.

quote: [lint] select = [..., "UP", ...] (pyupgrade), target-version = "py314"
statement: In Python files, code must use modern syntax for Python 3.14 per ruff pyupgrade rules (UP).

quote: [lint] select = [..., "SIM", ...] (flake8-simplify)
statement: In Python files, code must pass ruff flake8-simplify rules (SIM).

quote: [lint] select = [..., "ANN"] (flake8-annotations)
statement: In Python files, functions must have type annotations on arguments and return values (ruff ANN).

quote: [lint] ignore = ["EXE002"]
statement: In mini-project Python packages, ruff rule EXE002 (executable file without shebang) is turned off.

quote: "suspicious": { "noExplicitAny": "error" }
statement: In JS/TS files, code must not use an explicit `any` type (Biome noExplicitAny at error).

quote: linters: enable: - errorlint
statement: In Go files, error wrapping and comparison must use `errors.Is`/`errors.As` and `%w` rather than `==` or type assertions on errors (errorlint).

quote: linters: enable: - gocritic
statement: In Go files, code must pass gocritic checks.

quote: linters: enable: - revive
statement: In Go files, code must pass revive style checks (exported-symbol comments, naming, etc.).

quote: # misspell is left out on purpose: comments here are bilingual, and it reports Portuguese words such as "algoritmos" or "processos" as misspelled English.
statement: In the root Go lint config, the misspell linter is deliberately not enabled because comments are multilingual.

quote: enable: - misspell ... settings: misspell: ignore-rules: [problemas, candidatas, componentes, algoritmos, calcularon, recorre, representaciones]
statement: In several Go mini-projects, misspell is enabled with module-specific ignore-rules for Portuguese/Spanish words.

quote: "strict": true
statement: In TypeScript projects, code must compile under TypeScript `strict` mode.

quote: "noUncheckedIndexedAccess": true
statement: In TypeScript projects, indexed access results must be treated as possibly `undefined` and checked (noUncheckedIndexedAccess).

quote: cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings
statement: In Rust mini-projects, code must produce no clippy warnings (warnings are errors).

quote: No unrequested abstractions: no interface with one implementation, no factory for one product, no config for a value that never changes.
statement: In all code, there must be no interface with only one implementation, no factory for a single product, and no configuration for a value that never changes.

quote: Mark deliberate simplifications that cut a real corner with a known ceiling (global lock, O(n²) scan, naive heuristic) with a `ponytail:` comment naming the ceiling and upgrade path
statement: In all code, deliberate simplifications with a known ceiling must be marked with a `ponytail:` comment naming the ceiling and the upgrade path.

quote:
- No abstractions for single-use code.
- No "flexibility" or "configurability" that wasn't requested.
- No error handling for impossible scenarios.
statement: In all code, there should be no abstractions for single-use code, no unrequested configurability and no error handling for impossible scenarios.

quote: Parameterize every query. Never build SQL, NoSQL, or shell commands from input strings.
statement: In code that talks to databases or shells, queries must be parameterized and SQL, NoSQL or shell commands must never be built by concatenating input strings.
scope: ** database and shell-calling code (outside deliberate vulnerable lab code)

quote: **Never use `eval()` or `innerHTML`** with user-provided data
statement: In JS/TS code, `eval()` and `innerHTML` must never be used with user-provided data.

quote: **Never store sessions in client-accessible storage** (localStorage for auth tokens)
statement: In front-end code, auth tokens and sessions must never be stored in `localStorage` or other client-accessible storage.

quote: **Never log sensitive data** (passwords, tokens, full credit card numbers)
statement: In all code, logging calls must never include passwords, tokens, secrets, full card numbers or full PII.

quote: **Never expose stack traces** or internal error details to users
statement: In HTTP handlers, error responses must never expose stack traces or internal error details to users.

quote: CORS restricted to an explicit origin list from configuration. Never `*` with credentials.
statement: In HTTP servers, CORS must be restricted to an explicit origin list from configuration and must never use `*` with credentials.

quote: Hash passwords with bcrypt (≥12 rounds), scrypt, or argon2. The session secret comes from the environment, never from code.
statement: In authentication code, passwords must be hashed with bcrypt (>=12 rounds), scrypt or argon2, and session secrets must be read from the environment, never hard-coded.

quote: **Use httpOnly, secure, sameSite cookies** for sessions
statement: In server code setting session cookies, cookies must be `httpOnly`, `secure` and `sameSite`.

quote: Labels must come from small, fixed sets (route template, status class, provider name). Never use user IDs, raw URLs, error messages, or other unbounded values as labels
statement: In metrics instrumentation, metric labels must come from small fixed sets and must never be user IDs, raw URLs, error messages or other unbounded values.

quote: **Avoid prop drilling deeper than 3 levels.** If you're passing props through components that don't use them, introduce context or restructure the component tree.
statement: In React components, props should not be drilled through more than 3 levels of components that do not use them.

quote: Use semantic color tokens: `text-primary`, `bg-surface`, `border-default` — not raw hex values
statement: In UI code, colours should use semantic color tokens, not raw hex values.

quote: | Abbreviated names | `usr`, `cfg`, `btn`, `evt` | Use full words unless the abbreviation is universal (`id`, `url`, `api`) |
statement: In all code, identifiers should use full words rather than abbreviations like `usr`, `cfg`, `btn`, `evt`, except universal ones (`id`, `url`, `api`).

quote: **Don't mix patterns.** If some endpoints throw, others return null, and others return `{ error }` — the consumer can't predict behavior.
statement: In an API or module interface, error signalling must follow one consistent pattern (throw vs. return null vs. return `{ error }`), not a mix.

quote: Prefer real implementations > fakes > stubs > mocks. Mock only at boundaries where real deps are slow or non-deterministic
statement: In tests, real implementations should be preferred over fakes, stubs and mocks; mocks should be used only at boundaries where real dependencies are slow or non-deterministic.
